passages.note: Bill overview lists Payne as a co-sponsor of the Arizona empowerment scholarship accounts bill, signed as Chapter 388.
House Third Reading vote page shows Payne voting Y on a divided 31-26 passage, so the vote is not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Chapter text prints the operative expansion making every student eligible to enroll in an Arizona public school a qualified student; it names no voter.

rows.reasoning: Payne co-sponsored and voted Y on HB2853 (2022), a single-subject empowerment scholarship account bill whose new section 15-2401.01 makes "qualified student" include every resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in kindergarten or "Any of grades one through twelve", with the department transferring the student's own state funding into the account. That universal eligibility, usable for "Tuition or fees at a qualified school" (a nongovernmental school) and for "Services provided by a public school", matches the rung "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family" and excludes the rung limited to "most families". Payne acted on the bill as a State Representative in the same legislature, so the record counts for his current Senate seat.
